verdict.reasoning: Patient reports a 'really bad headache, had it for about a day now' and 'mainly on the left side' that is 'kind of throbbing'.

Patient says 'ever since yesterday morning, since I woke up really' and that it 'sort of comes and goes' and when asked if it completely goes away says 'just kind of fades, so it's still there a little bit'.

Patient notes 'quite sensitive to light' and later that it 'seems to be worse, when I'm in a light room or like sunlight. So I've kind of just been staying in as much as possible' and also says it 'seems to be better' when lying down.
When asked 'Is it worse when you lie flat, or when you bend forward?' patient replies 'no' and says lying down is better; to 'Any problems if you cough or sneeze?' patient replies 'no'.

Patient denies 'any problems with your eyes, or your eyesight', 'Any abnormal smells or tastes?', 'Any, any nausea, vomiting?', reports no feverish or cold symptoms ('No, not really any sort of, cold symptoms'), has not checked temperature but doesn't feel feverish, and denies 'weakness, tingling, numbness in your arms or legs'.
Patient states 'taken some painkillers' and later clarifies 'just Paracetamol'.
When asked about triggers, patient says 'may have been a bit stressed out at work, that kind of thing'.
Patient says she takes 'Microgynon, pill' and when asked when she started replies 'about six years ago'.
Transcript confirms current use of paracetamol ('just Paracetamol') but does not state that it is generally taken as needed as a chronic or PRN medication.
Patient states 'I'm allergic to Aspirin' and when asked what happens says 'I just feel really sick', indicating nausea with aspirin.
Patient reports 'my mum had, uh, high blood pressure, and she's got a history of migraines.'
Patient says she lives 'just with housemates, um, just friends', drinks 'a few drinks at the weekend', and answers 'No' to both 'do you smoke?' and 'Do you take any other drugs of any sort?'.
Headache is new and unilateral with photophobia ('mainly on the left side', 'quite sensitive to light'); doctor states 'it does, sound quite like a migraine'.

Doctor specifically inquires about and confirms Microgynon pill use ('Which contraception do you take?' ... 'Microgynon, pill' started 'about six years ago'), indicating it is taken into account in assessment.
Patient reports 'I'm allergic to Aspirin' with feeling 'really sick', and this is implicitly part of the clinical assessment as it guides analgesia choice.
Doctor advises 'taking, uh, um, some anti-inflammatories, along with the Paracetamol' and later patient reiterates 'I'll take some Ibuprofen and I'll um, hopefully, be a bit better'.
Doctor advises 'Make sure you're really well hydrated' but does not advise resting in a dark room; patient self-reports staying in and avoiding light but this is not given as part of the plan.

Doctor instructs to contact them if 'it isn't settling, or it's getting worse, or you get any other change in your headache. Um, or you're unwell with it, with a high temperature' and later adds 'If you have a raised temperature or, your headache's just getting worse, or you develop any rashes or anything like that. Then we'd need to speak to you straight away.' New neurological symptoms are covered earlier by screening for weakness/tingling/numbness and 'any other change in your headache'.

Doctor states 'I would, try and arrange to get your blood pressure checked, if you haven't had it checked for a while' and 'thing to do is to have a thermometer at home, so you can make sure that your temperature's OK.'

Doctor advises re-discussion if 'you're getting persistent, um, headaches, or headaches associated with your menstrual cycle, or certain things seem to trigger these headaches,' but does not mention starting a headache diary.
